title: Ahiram sarcophagus
description: The coffin of a king of Byblos carries the earliest long inscription in the Phoenician alphabet, the script from which the Greek and Latin alphabets descend.

title: Tyrians found Carthage
description: Settlers from Tyre found the colony in North Africa that becomes the leading Phoenician city of the western Mediterranean.

title: Siege of Tyre
description: Alexander the Great builds a causeway to the island city and takes it after seven months, ending Tyre's independence.

title: Beirut becomes a Roman colony
description: Veterans of two legions are settled at Berytus, which grows into a Roman city later known for its school of law.

title: Beirut earthquake
description: An earthquake and tsunami wreck the cities of the Phoenician coast and destroy Beirut and its law school.

title: Crusaders take Tripoli
description: The city surrenders after a blockade of several years and becomes the capital of the County of Tripoli, the last of the Crusader states to be founded.

title: Crusaders take Tyre
description: Tyre surrenders to the army of Jerusalem and a Venetian fleet, giving the Crusaders the last major port on the coast.

title: Mamluks take Tripoli
description: Sultan Qalawun storms and destroys the Crusader city, and a new Tripoli is built inland.

title: Mamluk campaign in Kisrawan
description: A Mamluk army subdues the Shia, Alawite and Druze mountaineers of Kisrawan, after which the district is gradually resettled by Maronites.

title: Battle of Anjar
description: The Druze emir Fakhr al-Din II defeats and captures the Ottoman governor of Damascus, the height of his power over Mount Lebanon and its neighbours.

title: Battle of Ain Dara
description: The Qaysi faction under the Shihab emirs defeats the Yamani Druze, many of whom leave for the Hauran, and the Shihabs become masters of Mount Lebanon.

title: Bashir II deposed
description: After British, Austrian and Ottoman forces drive the Egyptian army from the coast, the emir who had ruled Mount Lebanon for half a century surrenders and goes into exile.

title: Civil war in Mount Lebanon
description: Fighting between Druze and Maronites ends in the killing of thousands of Christians in towns such as Deir al-Qamar and Zahle, and prompts European intervention.

title: Mount Lebanon made a self-governing district
description: The Ottoman government and the European powers agree that Mount Lebanon will be governed by a Christian governor with a council of all the communities.

title: Syrian Protestant College opens
description: American missionaries open the school that becomes the American University of Beirut, a centre of the Arabic cultural revival.

title: Great Famine of Mount Lebanon
description: A wartime blockade, requisitions and a plague of locusts cause a famine that kills about 200,000 people, perhaps half the population of the mountain.

title: Greater Lebanon proclaimed
polity: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
description: The French general Henri Gouraud proclaims a state that joins Beirut, Tripoli, the south and the Beqaa to Mount Lebanon, within the borders of the present country.

title: Independence
description: France releases the Lebanese president and ministers it had arrested for ending the mandate, the day kept as independence day.

title: American marines land at Beirut
description: During an armed revolt against President Camille Chamoun the United States sends troops at his request, and the crisis ends with the election of a new president.

title: Civil war begins
description: Gunmen attack a church and Phalangist militiamen then kill the passengers of a bus carrying Palestinians, starting fifteen years of civil war.

title: Syrian army enters Lebanon
description: Syrian troops intervene in the civil war, beginning a military presence that lasts twenty-nine years.

title: Israel invades Lebanon
description: Israeli forces advance to Beirut and besiege the city until the Palestine Liberation Organization leaves, then occupy the south for eighteen years.

title: Sabra and Shatila massacre
description: Christian militiamen kill hundreds or thousands of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians in an area of Beirut surrounded by the Israeli army.

title: Beirut barracks bombings
description: Two truck bombs kill 241 American and 58 French servicemen of the multinational force, which leaves Lebanon within months.

title: Taif Agreement
description: Lebanese members of parliament agree to share power equally between Christians and Muslims, the basis for ending the civil war the following year.

title: Israel withdraws from the south
description: Israeli forces leave the zone they had held since 1982, and Hezbollah takes control of the border area.

title: Assassination of Rafic Hariri
description: A truck bomb kills the former prime minister and 21 others, setting off mass protests against the Syrian presence.

title: Syrian troops leave
description: The last Syrian soldiers cross the border after the protests known as the Cedar Revolution, ending twenty-nine years of military presence.

title: Lebanon War of 2006
description: A Hezbollah raid across the border starts a war of thirty-four days with Israel that kills more than a thousand people, most of them Lebanese.

title: Mass protests begin
description: Plans for new taxes bring hundreds of thousands into the streets against the political class, and the prime minister resigns as a financial crisis begins.
